note: Every table in public must appear here. A table in neither list fails supabase/tests/tenancy-tables.test.mjs, which is the point: a new table has to be classified at review time rather than discovered after Stage 4 makes it invisible.

buckets.tenant: Gets tenant_id in Stage 3 and a tenant isolation policy in Stage 4.
buckets.platform: Infrastructure and the global catalogue. Not owned by any tenant, so no tenant_id.
buckets.tenancy: The tenancy tables themselves. They define the boundary rather than sitting inside it: tenants.id IS the tenant and the other two name it directly, so none of them gains a tenant_id in Stage 3. They do get isolation policies in Stage 4.

identity.user_roles: Platform-level roles. Tenant-level role lives on tenant_members.
identity.users: One person, one account, across every tenant. What varies per tenant is the membership row, not the account.

platform.email_failures: Delivery diagnostics for the platform operator.
platform.products: The product catalogue, added in migration 0033. The same nine rows for every tenant, which is why it is not tenant-owned. Which products a given tenant has is tenant_products, in the tenancy bucket.
platform.rate_limits: Abuse control for the whole install, keyed by bucket and key. Not a tenant record.

tenancy.tenants: One row per business. Added in migration 0034.
tenancy.tenant_members: Membership and the role held in it. The spine: role moves off users.primary_role onto this row, because admin is a fact about a person in a tenant.
tenancy.tenant_products: Which products a tenant has switched on, and the settings for each. Carries tenant_id already, so Stage 3 skips it; Stage 4 still gives it a policy.

uniqueConstraints.note: Computed from pg_constraint over the tenant-owned and tenancy tables. Every one must be listed, so a new unique constraint is classified when it is written rather than discovered when two tenants collide.

needsTenantId.campaigns(code): A code is unique per business, not per platform.
needsTenantId.cashflow_months(month,scenario): Every tenant has its own January.
needsTenantId.cities(name): Two businesses may both run a Chennai chapter.
needsTenantId.complaints(ref): The C- series restarts per business.
needsTenantId.data_fields(table_name,column_name): Each tenant documents the same table for itself.
needsTenantId.email_templates(key): Every tenant wants its own host_invite template.
needsTenantId.employee_module_access(user_id,section): user_id is global, so one person in two tenants would get one grant row for both. The sharpest of these.
needsTenantId.employee_profiles(user_id): One profile per person per tenant, not per person.
needsTenantId.kpi_values(kpi_id,period): kpi_id is tenant-owned so this is nearly safe, but the pair is cheap to extend and keeps the index aligned with every read.
needsTenantId.membership_plans(tier): Each business defines its own Gold.
needsTenantId.newsletter_subscribers(email): One address may subscribe to two businesses.
needsTenantId.promo_codes(code): LAUNCH50 belongs to whoever issued it.
needsTenantId.reviews(period_type,period_start): One review per period per business.

alreadySafe.registrations(ticket_code): Deliberately global. The door scanner looks a ticket up by code alone, so codes must not repeat across tenants.
alreadySafe.sop_acknowledgements(version_id,user_id): version_id is tenant-owned, which scopes the pair.
alreadySafe.tenant_members(tenant_id,user_id): Includes tenant_id by construction, which is what lets one person belong to two tenants.
alreadySafe.tenants(slug): Deliberately global. A slug identifies a tenant across the whole platform, so this is one of the few unique constraints that must NOT be scoped to a tenant.
alreadySafe.user_badges(user_id,badge_id): badge_id is tenant-owned, which scopes the pair.

forceRlsNote: FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY is on 0 of 91 tables. Without it the table owner bypasses RLS entirely, which this project has already been bitten by: a permission test once passed while proving nothing because it ran as the owner. On a single-tenant system that was an embarrassing test. Under tenancy it is a leak. Stage 4 drives this to the full tenant-owned set; the guard only refuses to let it go down.
